target_customer: Primary care clinics, health systems and payers needing diabetic eye exams
problem: Preventable blindness from diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, with manual fundus review by ophthalmologists being costly and slow.
business_model: B2B value based retinal screening service with portable camera, tele-ophthalmology and AI

founders.name: Ankur Gupta
founders.background_notes: Ophthalmologist with healthcare venture capital experience; another profile lists him as co-founder and advisor.

founders.name: Ted Leng
founders.background_notes: Stanford ophthalmology professor and medical informatics director.

founders.name: Rishab Gargeya
founders.background_notes: No biography listed on YC page.

competitors.name: IDx
competitors.what: Autonomous AI diabetic retinopathy detection (IDx-DR) for primary care
competitors.traction_then: Pivotal trial enrolled 900 patients at 10 primary care sites January to July 2017

competitors.name: Eyenuk (EyeArt)
competitors.traction_then: Preregistered trial NCT03112005 began April 2017 with 942 patients at 15 sites

technical_complexity.rationale: Medical imaging AI, portable camera hardware and clinical validation, with regulatory clearance as a further hurdle.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical validation and care delivery integration could be hard to replicate; no FDA authorization for Spect was listed in one directory.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: IDx-DR was FDA cleared in April 2018; Spect was still operating through at least 2024 with a DocGo partnership.

market_need_then: YC page cites about 415 million diabetic patients at risk of retinopathy, and screening gaps in primary care were a recognized unmet need.

branding.domain_note: Used getspect.com (prefixed domain); the site blocked fetch with HTTP 403.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and mission focused around preventing blindness

brand_strength.rationale: No brand level press or community found; name resembles many Spectrum and Spec companies.

pivots.from: Retinal screening camera and AI in primary care
pivots.to: Mobile and at-home eye exams and tele-ophthalmology services
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from 2021 to 2023 coverage and not confirmed as a pivot

outcome_analysis: Spect was a YC S17 retinal screening company led by an ophthalmologist and a Stanford professor, which raised a 3.5 million dollar seed in late 2021 and partnered with DocGo in 2024. YC lists it as Inactive but no shutdown or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public. Its record shows founder domain fit but little evidence of scaled traction.
notes: YC status Inactive but the company was active in 2024 per a DocGo partnership noted by a directory; no end date found, exit type unknown. CB Insights lists a $1.5M seed Nov 2021 and $3.7M total; StartupIntros lists $4M; press says $3.5M. Competitor traction dates come from trial enrollment periods in later papers and press, not launch coverage from 2017.
